issues: Carry-over from iter67/68: auth-email-input remains `readonly` while device-key generates, blocking Playwright fill. Only impacts E2E/autofill, not the manual user flow. Recommend tracking device-key readiness via a React state flag instead of DOM-level readonly that snaps back on every remount.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py /auth/disconnect-soft (lines 475-503) correctly: (a) accepts token via cookie OR Authorization Bearer OR ?t= query param (essential for sendBeacon), (b) pushes last_seen_at 24h into the past (>> 35s threshold), (c) wraps DB update in try/except so a malformed beacon never errors out the response, (d) always returns 200 since sendBeacon discards the body. Solid.

server.py /webauthn/enroll-begin (lines 5187-5221) — anonymous endpoint, no signature required. Persists challenge with kind='signup' bound to a 32-char options_token. Correctly extracts rp_id from origin/referer header. No rate limit yet — consider adding one (e.g. 10/min/IP) to avoid challenge-flood DoS on the webauthn_challenges collection.

server.py /auth/register biometric block (lines 863-907): clean branching webauthn vs iris, iris hashes filtered to 20-128 char strings then sliced to 3. Note: no rejection if 4+ hashes provided (only 3 kept) — acceptable but worth a comment.

server.py line 1390: `recent_threshold = now - timedelta(seconds=35)` — aligns with 30s heartbeat tick (5s safety margin). Tighter than iter68's 60s; combined with /disconnect-soft this means a closed tab is stale in <35s (immediately on close if beacon fires).
Login.js signup payload (lines 333-336): correct conditional shape per biometric kind. Validation guard at line 318 ensures iris has 3 hashes before submit.
BiometricEnrollmentField.jsx error path: 'Impossible d'accéder à la caméra. Vérifie les permissions.' confirmed via runtime test with getUserMedia denied. data-testid='bio-error' renders correctly.
WARNING — server.py is now 7700 lines (+129 vs iter68). Splitting per-domain routers (auth, webauthn, devices, projects, chat, admin) is increasingly overdue.
